result.topic_en: A Landen/Gauss-type transformation of the elliptic integral ∫dT/√(aa sin²T + bb cos²T) through a chain of tangent substitutions involving successive constants a, b; a', b'; a'', b''.
result.transcription:
Math. 25 (61) [-7741-] 10

Setzt man
$\mathrm{tg}\, T \sqrt{\frac{a}{b}} = \mathrm{tg}\, T'$
$\mathrm{tg}\, 2T' \sqrt{\frac{a'}{b'}} = \mathrm{tg}\, 2T''$
$\mathrm{tg}\, 4T'' \sqrt{\frac{a''}{b''}} = \mathrm{tg}\, 4T'''$
u. s. w.
so wird
$\int \frac{dT}{\sqrt{(aa \sin T^2 + bb \cos T^2)}} = \int \frac{dT'}{\sqrt{(a'a' \sin 2T'^2 + b'b' \cos 2T'^2)}} = \int \frac{dT''}{\sqrt{(a''a''[?] \sin 2T''^2 + b''b'' \cos 2T''^2)}}$
auch ist
$\frac{\sin 2T}{\sqrt{(aa \sin T^2 + bb \cos T^2)}} = \frac{\sin 2T'}{\sqrt{(a'a' \sin 2T'^2 + b'b' \cos 2T'^2)}}$

methods.what: Chain of tangent substitutions defining successive transformed amplitudes
Invariance of the elliptic integral under the transformation (Landen/AGM-type transformation)
Accompanying algebraic identity relating sin 2T and sin 2T' under the transformation

items.quote:
so wird
$\int \frac{dT}{\sqrt{(aa \sin T^2 + bb \cos T^2)}} = \int \frac{dT'}{\sqrt{(a'a' \sin 2T'^2 + b'b' \cos 2T'^2)}}$
items.english: then the integral ∫dT/√(aa sin²T + bb cos²T) becomes equal to ∫dT'/√(a'a' sin²2T' + b'b' cos²2T'), and so on.

items.quote:
auch ist
$\frac{\sin 2T}{\sqrt{(aa \sin T^2 + bb \cos T^2)}} = \frac{\sin 2T'}{\sqrt{(a'a' \sin 2T'^2 + b'b' \cos 2T'^2)}}$
items.english: also sin 2T/√(aa sin²T + bb cos²T) = sin 2T'/√(a'a' sin²2T' + b'b' cos²2T').
